targets.authors: Espin C. A., van den Bosch R. M., van der Liende M., Rippe R. C., Beutick M., Langa A., Mol S. E.
targets.title: A systematic review of CBM professional development materials: Are teachers receiving sufficient instruction in data-based decision-making?
targets.evidence_quote: The purpose of this study was to conduct a conceptual replication of the Espin et al. systematic review through an analysis of CBM content in practitioner journal articles.
targets.outcome_quote: Results revealed a pattern similar to the one found by Espin et al. with approximately 18% of the content of practitioner articles on CBM devoted to the topic of decision-making. While, in their review of CBM PD materials, Espin et al. found the greatest proportion of attention was given to conducting CBM (53%) followed by general CBM information (24%), in the case of practitioner journal content, the greatest proportion of text was devoted to general CBM information (42.16%) followed by information on conducting CBM (39.29%).
targets.outcome_reasoning: The central underrepresentation of DBDM agrees, but the authors explicitly contrast the relative ordering of the other tested content categories and describe another difference in the Other category. The abstract comparison confirms a particular pattern; it is not an overall verdict encompassing all category comparisons. New sampled practitioner articles make this an empirical content-analysis replication despite the systematic-review title.

reasoning: New corpus of practitioner articles tests the specific four-category content pattern from Espin et al. (2021). The primary finding concerns representation of DBDM; the paper also explicitly compares the ordering of the other coded categories. Full text and reference list present.
